newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot, Boeing sign $400 million 10-plane deal.
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot, Boeing sign $400 million 10-plane deal.

text.p: Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines signed a final deal on Wednesday to pay Boeing Co. $400 million for 10 737-400 passenger jets.
This is the first purchase of Boeing jets by a Russian carrier. Russian companies often lease foreign planes.
Aeroflot Acting Chief Executive Valery Okulov said at the signing ceremony the first of the planes would be delivered in April 1998.

"A loan from the U.S.'s Chase Manhattan will finance 85 percent (of the cost), and Aeroflot will cover the remaining 15 percent with its own funds," Okulov said. The deal is Aeroflot's second major purchase without government backing, he said.
Boeing Executive Vice President Richard Albrecht said assembly of the first aircraft would begin next week.
"We hope that all the planes will be delivered according to schedule," he said.
The Boeing 737-400s will replace short-range Tupolev Tu-134 jets on Aeroflot domestic and international routes.
Okulov said Boeing jets would allow Aeroflot to improve air safety and profit margins.
Aeroflot will announce a fleet modernisation programme next week, he said.
